title: Figure 2. Distinct finite responses to local polarity challenges
role: Similar size-dependent reversal behavior can arise through distinct mechanisms, which predict different observable responses to polarity challenges.
status: provisional author-review candidate; main emphasis remains revisable

assets.caption: Finite native activation and withdrawal responses

legend: A–B: Actual peak activity in the physical right-hand cue footprint [L−3,L] at L19 (gray reference) and L39 (model colour). Each model uses the same requested physical support 3, peak and 1000-unit duration across those sizes: WP 0.1, Goryachev 6.4, followed by 13000 cue-free native units. Both inputs add stimulus×inactive to active, with equal loss from inactive. Time is linear through 1000 then logarithmic, with withdrawal marked at 1000; the final coordinate 14000 is 13000 after withdrawal. Concentrations are native and are never independently peak-normalized. Goryachev L39 develops a positive peak 11.7598; it is 10.581 at 10 off and 5.2796 at 100 off, then approximately zero by 1000 off. Its L19 reference instead grows to 61.676 after an initial small withdrawal dip. WP's two sizes have nearly equal challenger height, including cue-end peaks 1.5460/1.5434, despite different remaining incumbents.

C–D: Exact L39 spatial fields initially, at withdrawal, and after 13000 cue-free units. Purple shading is the physical cue footprint, not activity extent. Dotted horizontal lines give each case's initial background-plus-half-range threshold. WP39 retains two connected above-threshold domains in every saved off-frame (2027 samples); their final initial-side/challenged-side widths are 6.7382/5.2372. Goryachev L39 never forms a challenger above its initial half-contrast 58.695, but its positive cue-driven activity is explicitly visible in B and in the withdrawal profile. Its initial-side peak recovers from 100.052 at withdrawal to 117.390. Profile values are measured fields, not evidence inferred from a scalar-strength gate. The endpoint two-field comparisons in the source table remain distinct from any scalar criterion. Connected regions refer to spatial patterns, not tracked identities or protrusions.

E–G: All 97 retained basal checkpoints, with excess amount, connected half-contrast width and peak concentration divided by the value at each model's own reference size. Sizes use L/Lref (WP/Goryachev/deBelly Lref 19; Holmes 20; Spring resting L₀ref 1). Amount is the one-dimensional excess-concentration integral within the basal half-contrast core, not calibrated molecule number. Spring uses its actual physical domain for widths/amounts; deBelly retains nominal chemical-solver coordinates. Thirteen ineligible preparations remain in the linked table, without artificial zero values. At L19→39, WP's excess amount/width/peak folds are 2.124/2.042/1.000, versus Goryachev 2.152/1.119/1.903. All five curves and the original full native-unit organization artwork remain accessible.

The labels linking organization to response name conditional model predictions, not unique molecular identification or a causal allocation of reversal time. The native channels, doses, spatial discretization and clocks are not optical-actuator or reporter calibrations. The chemical grid has 201 cells at both sizes; the sampled input peak is 0.999388/0.997422 of the requested peak at L19/L39 (about 0.2% mismatch), while its physical integral is nearly unchanged. This small cue-sampling mismatch does not bound basal or other discretization errors; Goryachev L39's initial core has four sample centres and spatial convergence is not established by the retained checks. Thirteen thousand units of off-follow-up do not prove an asymptotic attractor. No velocity law or cell displacement is inferred. Small-loss recovery, analytic gain and evolved interventions remain supporting evidence, not the experimental headline.
narrative: Incumbent growth takes different spatial forms: most models widen; Goryachev grows taller and lowers available inactive substrate.

Under the native stimulus-times-inactive channel, Goryachev has weaker size-dependent challenger activity; its L39 response is positive and later decays. WP has nearly size-invariant challenger height but a larger remaining incumbent domain at L39.

After withdrawal WP39 retains two observed active domains while Goryachev39 restores the initial-side pattern over the finite follow-up. These are native response routes, not unique mechanistic classifications.
measurements: Activity peak/integrated increment inside the actual physical cue support, with native scale and a fixed within-model cue schedule.
Incumbent concentration, half-contrast extent/edge retreat and activity beyond the cue, followed after withdrawal.
Basal excess amount, connected width and peak concentration, preserving all97 native checkpoints and explicit reference normalization.
limitations: Native stimulus channel, dose and timescale are not experimentally calibrated; no optical actuator or reporter model is selected.
Finite 13000-unit off observations do not establish asymptotic stability, site ancestry, whole-field replacement from a scalar gate, or a movement law.
Goryachev39 has four native sample centres in its incumbent core; the retained evidence is not a spatial-convergence demonstration.
Observed response signatures and organization do not uniquely identify molecular mechanisms or causally partition reversal resistance.
